ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *h₂en-der. Proto-Germanic *an Proto-West Germanic *ana Old English on Middle English on English on From Middle English on, from Old English on, an (“on, upon, onto, in, into”), from Proto-West Germanic *ana, from Proto-Germanic *ana (“on, at”), from Proto-Indo-European *h₂en- (“on, onto”).

From Old Norse ón, án (“without”), from Proto-Germanic *ēnu, *ēno, *ino (“without”), from Proto-Indo-European *ḗnu (“without”). Cognate with North Frisian on (“without”), Middle Dutch an, on (“without”), Middle Low German āne (“without”), German ohne (“without”), Gothic 𐌹𐌽𐌿 (inu, “without, except”). Unlikely to be related to Ancient Greek ἄνευ (áneu, “without”), which is likely akin to Proto-Germanic *sundraz instead (whence sunder).
From Japanese 音読み (on'yomi, literally “sound reading”).

senses.d: In the state of being active, functioning or operating.
ex: All the lights are on, so they must be home.

senses.d: Happening; taking place; being or due to be put into action.
ex: We had to ration our food because there was a war on.
Some of the cast went down with flu, but the show's still on.

senses.d: Of a person, used to express agreement to or acceptance of a proposal or challenge made by that person; most commonly with subject “you” (see you're on).
ex: "Five bucks says the Cavs win tonight." ―"You're on!"
If he wants a fight, he's on!

senses.d: Fitted; covering or being worn.
ex: Your feet will soon warm up once your socks are on.
I was trying to drink out of the bottle while the top was still on!

senses.d: Of a stated part of something, oriented towards the viewer or other specified direction.
ex: The photograph shows the UFO side on.
edge on, side on, end on, face on

senses.d: Acceptable, appropriate.
ex: It's not fair to do that – it's just not on.
This kind of over-packaging of goods is completely not on.

senses.d: Possible; capable of being successfully carried out.
ex: Climbing up that steep ridge isn't on. We'll have to find another route.
He'd like to play the red next to the black spot, but that shot isn't on.

senses.d: Available; remaining.
ex: Smith is 25 points ahead with only 23 on.

senses.d: Having reached a base as a runner and being positioned there, awaiting further action from a subsequent batter.
Within the half of the field on the same side as the batsman's legs; the left side for a right-handed batsman.
ex: The captain moved two fielders to the on side.
Ponsonby-Smythe hit a thumping on drive.

senses.d: To an operating state.
ex: turn the television on

senses.d: So as to cover or be fitted.
ex: The lid wasn't screwed on properly.
Put on your hat and gloves.

senses.d: Along, forwards (continuing an action), onwards.
ex: The policeman moved the tramp on.
Drive on past the railway station.

senses.d: In continuation, at length.
ex: and so on
He rambled on and on.

senses.d: Later.
ex: Ten years on, nothing had changed in the village.

senses.d: Of betting odds, denoting a better-than-even chance. See also odds-on.
ex: That horse is twenty-to-one on, so you need to stake twenty pounds just to win one pound.

senses.d: Of a ball, into a pottable position.
ex: The black was previously unavailable, but in potting that red, he's now pushed the black on.

senses.d: Positioned at the upper surface of, touching from above.
ex: A vase of flowers stood on the table.
Please lie down on the couch.

senses.d: Positioned at or resting against the outer surface of; attached to.
ex: He had a scar on the side of his face.
There is a dirty smudge on this window.

senses.d: Covering.
ex: He wore old shoes on his feet.

senses.d: At or in (a geographical location or position).
ex: The lighthouse that you can see is on the mainland.
The suspect is thought to still be on the campus.

senses.d: At (a relative spatial position).
ex: We live on the edge of the city.
on the left, on the right, on the side, on the bottom

senses.d: Near; adjacent to; alongside; just off.
ex: The fleet is on the American coast.
Croton-on-Hudson, Rostov-on-Don, Southend-on-Sea

senses.d: Aboard (a mode of transport, especially public transport, or transport that one sits astride or uses while standing).
ex: on a bus, on a train, on a plane, on a ferry, on a yacht
on a bicycle, on a motorbike, on a horse, on a scooter

senses.d: In the direction of (some part of one's vessel), to within 45 degrees.
ex: A ship was sighted on the port quarter.
on the bow; on the starboard beam

senses.d: Expressing figurative placement, burden, or attachment.
ex: All of the responsibility is on him.
I put a bet on the winning horse.

senses.d: With verbs describing an action of pushing, pulling, pressing, etc., designates the thing to which force is applied.
ex: tug on the rope; push hard on the door

senses.d: To switch on.
ex: Can you on the light?

senses.d: Without.
In the Japanese language, a pronunciation, or reading, of a kanji character that was originally based on the character's pronunciation in Chinese, contrasted with kun.
ex: Most kanji have two kinds of reading, called "on" and "kun".

ety.text: Inherited from Middle French sur, from Old French sur, seur, sor, soure, souvre, sovre (“on, upon, over”), from Latin super (“over, on, above”). Doublet of super, a borrowing. Cognate with Old English ofer (“over, above”). More at over.

Inherited from Old Spanish sobre, from Latin super (“above”), from *eks-uper, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁eǵʰs (“out of”) (Latin ex) and *uperi (“above”), from *upo. Doublet of the borrowed super.

ety.text: From Old Galician-Portuguese sobre, from Latin super, from *eks-uper, which consists of Proto-Indo-European *eḱs (“out of”) and *uperi. Doublet of the borrowed super. Cognate to Spanish sobre, French sur, Ancient Greek ὑπέρ (hupér, “above”) and English over, super and sur-.

From Latin ad. In a few phrases, a stems from Latin ā, ab.
From Old Galician-Portuguese en, from Latin in (“in”), from Proto-Italic *en, from Proto-Indo-European *h₁én (“in”). Doublet of in.
